prompt: Complete a static paint method that sets a rectangular clip, floods the whole surface with blue so only the clipped window changes, then removes the clip and stamps a red corner marker.
explanation: A clip is a mask on the Graphics object: every drawing call is still issued, but pixels outside the clip shape are discarded, so flooding the whole surface only recolours the window. setClip(null) clears the mask so later drawing reaches the entire surface again -- which is why the red marker at the top-left corner appears even though it sits outside the earlier window. Clipping is how Swing keeps a repaint cheap: it clips to the damaged region before calling paintComponent.
hints: Paint the white background before you call setClip, or the background itself gets masked.
setClip(int, int, int, int) takes the same x, y, width, height as fillRect.
Pass null to setClip to remove the mask before drawing the red corner marker.
